1_1.summary: O Rudra, salutations to your anger, your arrow, your bow and your two arms. May these powerful forces be gracious toward us.

1_2.summary: O Rudra, let your arrow, bow and quiver be auspicious. With these gentle forms, bring us happiness and well-being.

1_3.summary: O Rudra, giver of peace from the mountain, look upon us through your gentle, auspicious form, which is free from terror and reveals purity.

words.meaning: Revealing what is free from evil

1_4.summary: O mountain-dwelling protector, make the arrow you hold ready to shoot harmless and auspicious. Do not injure people or the living world.

1_5.summary: O Lord of the mountain, we address you with words of peace. May all our world be free from illness and filled with goodwill.

1_6.summary: May Rudra, the foremost divine healer and advocate, speak in our favor, overcoming poisonous creatures and all hostile powers.

words.meaning: Advocate / one who speaks for us

1_7.summary: We behold the auspicious Rudra in the coppery, rosy and tawny sun. We seek to calm the anger of the countless Rudras present in every direction.

1_8.summary: Rudra, blue-necked and crimson, moves across the sky in the visible form of the sun. Cowherds, water carriers and all beings see him; may his presence bless us.

1_9.summary: Salutations to the blue-necked, thousand-eyed giver of blessings. I also bow to all his attendant powers.

1_10.summary: O blessed Lord, loosen the bowstring from both ends of your bow and put away the arrows in your hand.

1_11.summary: O thousand-eyed Lord with many quivers, unstring your bow and blunt the arrowheads. Be gentle and well-disposed toward us.

words.meaning: O bearer of a hundred quivers

1_12.summary: May the bow of the matted-haired Lord remain unstrung, his arrows lose their sharp points and power to harm, and his quiver be harmless.

1_13.summary: O most generous Lord, turn the weapon and bow in your hand into a harmless protection, guarding us on every side.

1_14.summary: Salutations to your mighty weapon held at rest, to both your arms, and to your bow.

1_15.summary: May the weapon of your bow pass us by on every side. Set your quiver far away from us.

2_1.summary: Salutations to the golden-armed commander, Lord of every direction.

2_2.summary: Salutations to Rudra in the green-leaved trees, the Lord of all creatures.

words.meaning: To the one who cannot be slain

words.meaning: To the counselor / knower of sacred counsel

words.meaning: To the sustainer / expander of the world

words.meaning: To the one with a loud voice
To the one who calls out

words.meaning: To the one who pervades all

words.meaning: To the one who strikes down

10_1.summary: O Rudra, punisher of evil, Lord of nourishment, detached and blue-red in form, do not frighten or harm our people and animals. May none of them perish or fall ill.

10_2.summary: O Rudra, your gracious form is healing at all times. Through that healing presence, bless us with life and well-being.

10_3.summary: We offer this prayer to mighty, matted-haired Rudra, whose power overcomes hostile forces. May people and animals flourish, and may everyone in our village be healthy and well nourished.

words.meaning: To the one who subdues opposing heroes

10_4.summary: O Rudra, be kind and grant us happiness. We worship your conquering power with reverence; under your guidance, may we receive the welfare that Manu, our forefather, sought.

words.meaning: To the subduer of opposing heroes

10_5.summary: O Rudra, spare our elders, children, youths and unborn children. Do not harm our fathers, mothers or the bodies dear to us.

10_6.summary: O Rudra, protect our children, descendants, lifespan, cattle and horses. Do not strike down our brave people in anger; we come to you with offerings and reverence.

10_7.summary: Keep your power to strike people and cattle far from us, O Rudra. Let your favor be ours: protect us, speak for us and grant us shelter and happiness.

words.meaning: To the power that strikes cattle
To the power that strikes people
To the subduer of opposing heroes

10_8.summary: Praise the renowned, ever-youthful Rudra, seated in his chariot, fierce like a formidable wild beast. As we praise you, be kind to us and let your forces strike elsewhere.

words.meaning: Seated in a chariot / dwelling in a recess

10_9.summary: May Rudra’s weapon and fierce displeasure pass us by. O generous Lord, relax your drawn weapons for those who offer worship, and be gracious to our children and descendants.

words.meaning: Of the one intent on harm

10_10.summary: O most generous and gracious Lord, be kindly disposed toward us. Place your weapon on the highest tree and approach us wearing your hide and bearing the Pinaka bow.

10_11.summary: O radiant red Lord who scatters blessings, I bow to you. Let your thousands of weapons fall elsewhere, away from us.

10_12.summary: For the countless Rudras dwelling on earth, we ask that their bows be unstrung and placed a thousand yojanas away, beyond the reach of harm.

words.meaning: At a distance of a thousand yojanas

11_1.summary: We invoke the Rudras who dwell in the atmosphere, vast as an ocean. The surrounding prayer asks that their weapons remain far from us.

11_2.summary: We invoke the blue-necked and fair-throated forms of Sharva who move beneath the earth, asking that their fierce power spare us.

11_3.summary: We invoke the blue-necked and fair-throated Rudras who dwell in heaven, asking for their benevolence.

11_4.summary: We invoke the Rudras dwelling in trees, golden-green, blue-necked and deep red in appearance.

11_5.summary: We invoke the Rudras who rule over beings, appearing with shaven heads or matted hair.

11_6.summary: We invoke the Rudras whose power can afflict people through what they eat and drink, and seek protection from that harm.

11_7.summary: We invoke the guardians of the paths, the Rudras who sustain us with food and fight to ward off danger.

11_8.summary: We invoke the armed Rudras who move through sacred fords and pilgrimage places, bearing sharp weapons and swords.

11_9.summary: All these Rudras, and the many more spread throughout every direction, are addressed together. May their bows be unstrung a thousand yojanas away from us.

words.meaning: At a distance of a thousand yojanas

11_10.summary: We bow with joined hands in every direction to the Rudras of earth, atmosphere and heaven, whose arrows act through food, wind and rain. May they be gracious; we entrust to their power those whom we oppose and those who oppose us.
